title: On graphs whose cycle space is spanned by their Hamilton cycles
summary: The cycle space of a graph $G$, denoted $\mathcal{C}(G)$, is a vector space over ${\mathbb F}_2$, spanned by all incidence vectors of edge-sets of cycles of $G$. If $G$ has $n$ vertices, then $\mathcal{C}_n(G)$ denotes the subspace of $\mathcal{C}(G)$, spanned by the incidence vectors of Hamilton cycles of $G$. We consider several known sufficient conditions for Hamiltonicity and show that an appropriate and fairly mild strengthening of each such condition in fact ensures the stronger property $\mathcal{C}_n(G) = \mathcal{C}(G)$.
